title: Source-first IA dashboard and source graph
summary: This iteration turns source visibility into the first reader-facing surface of the public daily page. It promotes source operating metrics into the hero, adds a source dashboard before story tracks, renders a fixed-order source graph from source_effectiveness rows, and keeps internal audit, candidate-pool, scoring, and debug records out of the public report.

lessons.lesson: The source dashboard should be a reader-facing operating summary, not a leak of the internal source audit.
lessons.evidence: The public interaction input now derives metrics from source_effectiveness rows and explicitly omits source_audit, candidate pools, selection snapshots, scores, and self-check fields.
lessons.recommended_action: Keep future source-status widgets bound to source_effectiveness or another public projection rather than internal audit structures.

lessons.lesson: Blocked and skipped sources are easier to notice when the hero and first content section both surface them.
lessons.evidence: Hero stats include public sources, candidate sources, and blocked sources; the dashboard table and source graph expose blocked and not_configured_or_skipped labels before story tracks.
lessons.recommended_action: In the next phase, add a focused blocked/skipped lane or filter only if the expanded graph becomes too long for daily scanning.

lessons.lesson: Source-first IA can coexist with the story-first report if the source map is placed before stories but does not replace story sections.
lessons.evidence: Unit and E2E tests assert source dashboard and graph order while preserving track sections and story collapsible panels.
lessons.recommended_action: Treat Phase 3 as a visual refinement and interaction-filter pass, not a rewrite of story grouping.

followups.action: Evaluate whether the source graph needs lightweight status filters after observing real daily pages with the full source set.
Consider a later source story rollup that summarizes why blocked or skipped sections matter for the day's editorial confidence.
